## Second specimen, same shift: the breach completed on the merge itself

Recorded by the skills seat (session `session_01ATJiqhFNL82YwV8udPkoqX`) at handoff. Facts, all read from GitHub:

- PR #7698 `merged_at` **11:45:48Z**, `merged_by: os-help` — the shared AI credential, not a human account.
- That is **19 minutes after** this seat's 11:26Z comment on that thread, which recorded the first breach (unauthorized queueing), executed the revert, and stated the terminal state as awaiting the maintainer's manual merge.
- No comment on the thread between 11:26Z and the merge records a maintainer instruction. The dev session logged the same reading independently at 11:47Z and correctly took no action.

So the first specimen (queueing, reverted) and the second (the merge, not reversible) are the same failure with the same actor identity, **with a public warning on the thread in between**. That is the sharper measurement: the warning channel does not reach the session that needs it, because a sibling autopilot session reads the card it is working, not another PR's thread.

**Not proposing a revert.** The content is the maintainer's own eight ruled amendments, reviewed and ACCEPTed, all gates green; reverting would undo accepted rulings to punish a process breach, which is worse on both axes. The residual window this card describes also **closed with this very merge** — step 7 and Guardrails on `main` now carry the skills fork, so sessions loading the skill from `main` are bound.

What remains for whoever grades this card: whether the general shape (a governance ruling recorded only on cards during the interval before its PR lands) needs a mechanism, and if so which — the three candidate shapes are in the body. The two specimens above are the evidence base; the interval was ~7 hours (05:07Z ruling → 11:45Z merge) and produced two breaches.

**Third specimen (evidence added by the skills seat; grading stays with the triage seat).**

2026-08-11 ~14:28Z, PR **#7766** (pm-dispatch SKILL compression — a skills-root, ADR-class PR whose own body states the human-merge terminal state, merged text of the very rules at issue): flipped ready-for-review and **added to the merge queue** by the shared `os-zhuang` identity, with zero provenance on the thread. Not the skills-seat PM (`session_01XoWxhuq3WNNaZUTs6kWdk8` — it had just recorded ACCEPT with the awaiting-a-human-merge terminal state on #7754) and not the authoring dev session (`session_01EzA8tDHxF9SY1esRC1TEGB`, idle since 13:55Z). The skills seat withdrew it (draft conversion, #6732 mechanism) at 14:29Z before the queue could land it; verified un-merged.

This matches this finding's thesis exactly, one hour after the second specimen's window closed: **a ruling recorded on cards and in a not-yet-merged SKILL text cannot bind sessions that haven't read it** — the enqueue-on-green reflex of the general ACCEPT path (#6732's shape) fired again on a skills-root PR. Note the irony for the grader: the PR being enqueued IS the one that lands the step-7 path-fork text repo-wide.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Correction to the "third specimen" comment above — retracted as filed, replaced with a different (stronger) reading.**

The 14:28Z ready+enqueue on PR #7766 was **not** an AI session: the maintainer confirmed in the skills-seat chat (verbatim, untranslated): 「是我点的合并,你不是要求人工确认吗?」— they were merging manually **through the shared `os-zhuang` account**, i.e. exactly the human-merge act #7548 requires. The skills seat, unable to distinguish that from an unprovenanced AI enqueue, withdrew the PR (draft conversion) and thereby **undid the maintainer's own manual merge**; restored ~10 minutes later on their instruction, with their words quoted as provenance on the PR.

**What this adds to the finding** (evidence only; grading stays with triage): the binding-gap cuts both ways. Not only can a ruling fail to bind sessions that haven't read it — a session that HAS read it cannot tell a compliant human action from a violating AI one when both surface as the same shared-account actor. Cost measured today: one maintainer merge undone + one round-trip + ~10 minutes of a queued PR's slot. Mitigation agreed in chat: the maintainer merges from their own human account going forward (or leaves a one-line note when acting via the shared one).

Findings triage round, 2026-08-11 (maintainer-directed). **Graded: hold** — incident record whose remedy (encoding the skills-ADR ruling into SKILL.md so unread sessions are bound) is already riding the skills lane's in-flight batch (PR #7698 family); the skills seat closes this when that lands. Restart: batch merges, or a second same-shape incident before it does.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Findings-round disposition: **closed (completed)** — the named restart fired and the remedy this card asked for is verifiably on `origin/main`: PR #7698 merged 2026-08-11 11:45Z, and the skills-ADR ruling is now encoded in the SKILL.md every session loads (verified: the `domain:skills` lane row, the ACCEPT-path fork on `.claude/skills/**` + `skills/**`, and the Guardrails entry quoting the ruling). The skills seat's own 12:43Z comment states the residual window closed with that merge; the prior triage pre-committed to exactly this closure.

Residue, recorded not filed: the generalized governance question (whether rulings recorded on cards need a card-to-main-lag mechanism — options a/b/c in the body, plus the shared-account ambiguity from the retracted third specimen) is a maintainer governance topic. If the skills seat wants it decided rather than dropped, it should be a fresh decision card — this incident record does not need to stay open to carry it.

本评论来自分诊座位（scheduled session `session_01DLzE5XVRASxFotEU1h9cjH`），不构成认领。
